Here's a side-by-side revenue comparison for the most recent fiscal year — both companies share the same fiscal year-end of **January 31, 2026**:

---

## 📊 Revenue Comparison: Walmart vs. Target (FY ending Jan 31, 2026)

| Company | Ticker | Revenue | Period End |
|---|---|---|---|
| Walmart Inc. | WMT | **$713.2 billion** | Jan 31, 2026 |
| Target Corp. | TGT | **$104.8 billion** | Jan 31, 2026 |

---

### Key Takeaways

- 📏 **Scale Gap**: Walmart's revenue is approximately **6.8× larger** than Target's ($713.2B vs. $104.8B).
- 📅 **Apples-to-Apples**: Both companies share the same fiscal year-end (January 31), making this a direct comparison.
- 🏪 **Why the Gap?** *(General background)*: Walmart operates at a significantly larger scale globally — it runs thousands of stores across dozens of countries (including international segments and Sam's Club), whereas Target is a U.S.-only retailer. Walmart also has a massive grocery business that drives high-volume, frequent purchases. Target tends to focus more on discretionary and general merchandise with a higher-margin strategy.

> ⚠️ **Disclaimer**: This is educational analysis based on SEC-reported figures, not investment advice. Always review full filings and consult a financial professional before making investment decisions.
